title: Probability of an extended walk
statement: Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space, and let the probability of a walk of length $k$ be defined by choosing its initial state uniformly and then taking transitions according to $A$. For every walk $g$ of length $k$ and state $j$, the probability of the walk obtained by appending $j$ is the probability of $g$ multiplied by the transition probability from its final state to $j$.
hypotheses_covered: Each row of A sums to one
g is a walk of length k
